title: Peer desk check
note: Hand-placed. Each card uses the page’s date. Silent is —, not Neutral. Does not vote.

houses.name: UBS CIO
houses.title: Stock outlook remains constructive
houses.assets: Global equities Attractive / IN; quality bonds further out the curve selective; commodities diversifier
houses.vsClause: Constructive equities through a shallow hike cycle vs Equities OUT.
houses.quote: we maintain our constructive outlook and expect the S&P 500 to move higher

houses.name: BlackRock Investment Institute
houses.title: Weekly market commentary
houses.assets: US and EM equities OW / IN; long UST UW / OUT; prefer short and medium bonds; selective credit
houses.vsClause: Closest full-axis match. Still challenges Equities OUT.
houses.quote: We remain pro-risk, but see little room for error

houses.name: Goldman Sachs AM
houses.title: International Market Pulse
houses.assets: Equities IN; duration Neutral; selective credit; TIPS as inflation hedge
houses.vsClause: Growth and Risk-on align. Inflation leaning cold is their path toward ~2% by 2027, not a now-print.
houses.quote: We remain constructive on equities as exceptional earnings

houses.name: Citi Wealth
houses.title: CIO Weekly Bulletin
houses.assets: Risk assets add-on-dips IN; long duration UW / OUT; commodities and precious metals IN
houses.vsClause: Agrees hot and strong. Calls policy easy (Taylor gap) while Rates is Tight; Equities IN vs OUT.
houses.quote: The macroeconomic data does not give the Fed room to ease

houses.name: 22V Research
houses.title: Economic Cycle Dynamics are Driving Rates
houses.assets: Risk-on / AI-services IN; retail and transports dialed back
houses.vsClause: Strong EPS and Risk-on vs Equities OUT.
houses.quote: We are not negative on risk assets UNLESS CPI/PPI come in unusually hot

houses.name: Apollo / Torsten Sløk
houses.title: Strong Jobs, Upside Risks to Next Week's CPI
houses.vsClause: Strong jobs and upside inflation, September hike.
houses.quote: we now expect the FOMC to raise interest rates at its September meeting

houses.name: Barclays Private Bank
houses.title: The debt and yield eclipse
houses.assets: Duration slightly below neutral (3–5y); long end vulnerable; BBB-/BB crossover IN
houses.vsClause: Resilient growth, hike pressure, and long-bond stress align. Inflation less clearly hot.
houses.quote: maintaining duration slightly below neutral, at around three to five years

houses.name: PIMCO
houses.title: If Inflation Is the Problem, Why Aren't Wages?
houses.vsClause: Expects core inflation to moderate; patient Fed vs Inflation leaning hot and Rates Tight.
houses.quote: We still expect core inflation to moderate over the coming months

houses.name: JPMorgan AM
houses.title: Global Asset Allocation Views 3Q 2026
houses.assets: Equities moderately OW (US/EM/JP); US HY OW; UST Neutral; long European duration
houses.vsClause: Same hot-skew, growth, and pro-risk. More dovish on the Fed (hold; market too hawkish) vs Rates Tight. Page is 9 Jul.
houses.quote: distribution of risks tilts toward an economy that is running too hot

agrees: Growth firm (strong / leaning strong) almost everywhere they spoke.
Inflation skews hot or upside risk, not done — PIMCO and GSAM are the dissent.
Long bonds are not a clean bid.
Most still call risk appetite Risk-on.
challenged: Equities OUT — hardest miss (GSAM, JPM, Citi, UBS, BlackRock, 22V still constructive).
Rates Tight — Citi calls policy Easy (Taylor gap); JPM AM more dovish (hold).
Inflation leaning hot — PIMCO and GSAM still expect moderation toward ~2%.
Liquidity — almost nobody names it. BlackRock scarcity / competition for capital is the closest echo.

closest.name: BlackRock
closest.clause: Tight cash language, lean-tight Rates, strong Growth, hot-skew Inflation, Risk-on — still OW equities.

scorecard.falsifier: Soft CPI/PCE and cooler labor that kills hike odds while earnings hold mid — stocks and long bonds bid together again.
